subject: Google Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash, Gemini API model gemini-omni-1.1-flash, August 27 2026
central_claim: Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash is a publishable AI engineering topic because official Google release notes, the Gemini API changelog, the model card, the model page and developer documentation support a bounded E2/R1 claim: Google has moved video generation toward an iterative API workflow with video extension, first-and-last-frame interpolation, resolution control and Interactions API state handling, while quality, speed and cost superiority remain vendor-authored and were not independently reproduced in this turn.

selection.reason: Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash is a fresh 2026-08-27 generally available model release with multiple official primary documents. It changes engineering decisions for teams adding generated video to products because the public API surface now includes interaction state, extension, interpolation, file delivery and resolution choices. The conclusion is bounded because this turn did not call the API, generate videos, inspect internal weights or independently measure quality, speed or cost.

claims.claim: Google released Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash as a GA Gemini API model that changes developer integration from one-shot video generation toward iterative video editing workflows through Interactions API state, video extension, first-and-last-frame interpolation and resolution control; the publishable claim is about documented API and model behavior, not independently proven video quality, speed or cost superiority.

Opened Google's 2026-08-27 Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash announcement. It described scene extension up to 40 seconds, first-and-last-frame control, 360p preview, 4K upscaling, Google AI Studio and Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform availability, and Google Flow/Gemini app availability. Used for announcement facts and feature discovery, not independent performance proof.

Opened Gemini API release notes. The 2026-08-27 entry confirms GA release of gemini-omni-1.1-flash, video extension, interpolation, resolution parameter values 360p/720p/1080p/4k, and deprecation of gemini-omni-flash-preview on 2026-09-30. Also reviewed nearby 2026-08-26 Gemini 3.5 Transcribe and 2026-08-13 Gemini 3.7 Flash entries as same-month alternatives.

Opened the Gemini Omni Flash model card updated/published 2026-08-27. It describes Gemini Omni Flash and Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash, lists text/image/audio/video inputs and video-with-audio output, native multimodal transformer architecture, training data categories, TPU/JAX/ML Pathways implementation context, known limitations around consistency, complex motion and text rendering, and speech-editing restrictions.

Opened the model page. It confirms model code gemini-omni-1.1-flash, supported data types for input text/image/video up to 10 seconds for editing and extension, output video, 1,048,576 token context window, 3-10 second output video at 360p/720p/1080p/4K and 24 FPS, stable/preview model names, August 2026 latest update and last updated 2026-08-27 UTC.

Opened the Omni developer guide. It documents text-to-video, image-to-video, first-and-last-frame interpolation, video editing, response_format resolution control, Interactions API response structure, URI delivery for videos larger than 4MB, File API upload/polling and Python/JavaScript/REST examples. Treated as implementation documentation but not as proof that the examples were executed in this turn.

Opened Google DeepMind's 2026-08-13 Gemini 3.7 Flash announcement and related changelog/model-card paths. It is a major coding and agent model release with engineering relevance, but it was older than the 2026-08-27 Omni GA and centered on Google-authored benchmark claims. Omni 1.1 had a fresher API workflow change with clearer developer integration details.

Opened the 2026-08-26 Gemini 3.5 Transcribe announcement and Gemini API changelog entry. It is relevant for speech-to-text products, including live transcription and custom vocabulary, but the editorial utility was narrower than Omni 1.1's multimodal video workflow shift.

Reviewed OpenAI official news paths around 2026-08-28, including the Cursor contract wind-down post, the Hugging Face incident post, GPT-5.6 Sol materials and API/changelog paths. These were important company, safety or access signals, but this pass did not find a fresher non-duplicate model/API/runtime artifact topic with stronger E2 engineering utility than Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash.

Reviewed Anthropic official news and release-note signals, including Claude's text watermark explanation, Claude Opus 5/Sonnet 5, Claude Code/web/browser-related product signals and system-card paths. Recent visible items were product or policy heavy and did not provide a stronger same-day E2 technical implementation story.

Reviewed Qwen blog and Hugging Face registry paths, DeepSeek GitHub/Hugging Face official paths and Mistral changelog. Qwen and Z.ai open-weight releases were already used by the 2026-08-27 and 2026-08-29 AI edition candidates, so this run avoided repeating those central claims. DeepSeek and Mistral paths did not surface a fresher official model/API/runtime item that beat the selected Google candidate.

Search results and secondary snippets were used only to discover official Google, OpenAI, Anthropic, Qwen, DeepSeek, Mistral and runtime-library paths. No article fact or central scoring decision relies on search snippets, social posts, community discussions or third-party summaries without opened primary-source confirmation.
